# PR #5146: Patch: a fork screen resumed after a cut inside an --extend batch plays that batch out, as an uncut run does

Closes #5123

A fork screen resumed from `--save` now decides each stop the way the uncut run does. A save cut inside an `--extend` batch plays out the rest of that batch instead of reading as finished. A finished save plays no game, including one stopped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of 20 live forks.

The change is in `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` only. I followed the plan without departing from it.

## What changed

- **Cause:** `resume_save` counted the live forks of every saved deal, including deals a cut batch left past `target`, before asking `next_batch` whether to stop. The uncut loop counts only up to each batch boundary.
- **`save_plan`:** a new pure function walks the batches from `initial_deals`, then `next_batch`'s, and counts only the live forks up to each boundary.
  - It returns `Some(boundary)` for the first batch the save leaves incomplete, or `None` for a finished save.
  - `resume_save` uses it for the finished check and for the stop after each batch it plays. The old `live_of` closure is gone.
  - `live_forks` is a small helper for one deal's live forks.
- **`next_batch`:** its doc comment now says `live` counts only the deals up to `games_done`. Its body is unchanged.
- **Ruling and untouched code:** R4607000's note is unchanged, so there is no new ruling and no `spec/pending` file. The no-`--save` path and `arena.rs` are untouched.

## Tests

Three new tests, all named `r4607000_…`, plus a `hand_map` helper that builds a hand-written save:

- **`r4607000_a_cut_inside_an_extended_batch_plays_the_rest_of_it`:** deals 1–215 with 18 live forks up to deal 200 and 2 more in the cut batch plan `Some(300)`. Completed to deal 300, the plan is `None`. Without `--extend` it is `None`.
- **`r4607000_a_cut_batch_without_live_forks_plans_as_before`:** a part-played batch with no live forks plans `Some(300)`, then `Some(400)` once whole. It also covers an empty map, a map one deal short of the first batch, 20 live forks stopping the screen at deal 200, and no `--extend`.
- **`r4607000_a_save_stopped_at_the_cap_plays_no_game`:**
  - The plan for 1–1999 is `Some(2000)` and for 1–2000 it is `None`.
  - A real `resume_save` over a 2000-deal save with `extend = true` makes no probe call, so not even the identity game is played.
  - The save file is byte-identical afterwards, and the tally reads 2000 forks.

# #5123: Patch: a fork screen resumed after a cut inside an --extend batch plays that batch out, as an uncut run does
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A change to the AI is kept or reverted on a long measurement, the fork screen. It can run for twelve hours or more, so it saves each finished game and picks up again after a crash or a bot run's time limit. One case is wrong today: the run is cut partway through an extra batch of games. The resumed run can then decide it is already finished and report on fewer games than an uninterrupted run would. Which games those are depends on timing. After the fix, a resumed screen always reports the same games and the same result as one that was never cut.

## Why

- **The ruling promises equal tallies.** R4607000 says “a screen played in pieces prints the tally line one uninterrupted run prints, byte for byte.”
- **`resume_save` breaks that** (`crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs:1016–1029` and `:1067`). `live_of` counts the live forks of every saved deal, including deals past `target` that a cut batch left behind. `next_batch(target, …)` then decides the stop at the old batch boundary with those forks counted.
- **A concrete case:** `--forks --extend --save s.jsonl` on improve-dev, 200 deals first.
  - Deals 1–200 hold 18 live forks, so the screen extends to deals 201–300.
  - It is cut after 15 of those are saved, and they hold 2 live forks.
  - On rerun, deals 1–200 are all present. `next_batch(200, 20, true, 200)` meets `screen_done` (20 ≥ `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED`), so the save reads as finished and the tally covers 215 deals.
  - The uncut loop (`fork_screen.rs:1170–1203`) plays whole batches and checks only after each one, so it tallies all 300.
  - The 15 deals kept are the ones that finished first, which favours short games, and a rerun after another cut would differ.
- **This is the documented path, not a corner.**
  - `training/improve.md` (A screen, step 3) tells an agent to pass `--save`, because a fork screen outlasts a bot's 150-minute model call (#4448's took about 12 and 16 core-hours) and the harness resumes it.
  - `--extend` is the choice for a change that acts rarely, whose first 200 deals hold under 20 live forks (#4595's screen read 20 forks over 200 games).
  - So for such a screen, a cut inside an extended batch is the likely case.
- **A smaller miss.** A finished save that stopped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of 20 live forks fails the finished check, so it plays the identity game again before reprinting. The ruling says a finished save plays nothing.
- **Untested.** The only test of the stop, `r4607000_extend_counts_saved_and_new_live_forks_together` (`fork_screen.rs:2054`), calls `next_batch` alone. No test resumes across a part-played batch.

## Proposal

- Decide each stop as the uncut run would. Walk the saved deals batch by batch (200, then 100 more at a time), and at each boundary count only the live forks of deals up to it. Stop at the first batch that is incomplete, or at the boundary where the screen stops.
- Use the same walk for the finished check, so a save capped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` reprints without the identity game.
- Put the plan (which deals to play next) in a pure function, and unit-test it on hand-written maps, as `r4607000_a_hand_written_save_reprints_its_tally_without_playing` does.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` (`resume_save`, `next_batch`) and its tests. R4607000's note stays as it is: the fix makes the code do what the note says, and its `proven_in` already names the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A save holding deals 1–200 with fewer than `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` live forks, plus some of deals 201–300 whose forks would push the count past it, plans the rest of 201–300 instead of reading as finished.
- [ ] A save whose part-played batch holds no live forks plans the same deals as today.
- [ ] A finished save plays no game, not even the identity game. This includes one stopped at `SCREEN_MAX_GAMES` short of the floor.
- [ ] The existing r4607000 tests pass, the new ones are named `r4607000_…`, and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools fork_screen`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are clean.

## Size and risks

Small: about 30 lines and three unit tests in one file, with no AI or engine change. Low risk. Screens without `--save` are untouched, and a save that never stopped inside an extended batch resumes exactly as today.
